title: AI now runs inside the bank, and so do the risks
dek: Barclays and Trust Bank show agentic AI doing real operational work this week, while a breach in Seoul and warnings from the ECB and Australia's central bank show why security and oversight need to keep pace.

body.head: From pilot to production
body.text: Barclays says most of its developers will be using Anthropic's Claude Code by the end of 2027, and its Global Markets business already routes 120,000 client emails a day through Claude models. In Singapore, Trust Bank's AI agents now triage IT incidents in about two minutes, down from 15 to 20, with 65% of the analysis immediately actionable before an engineer even joins the ticket. Both banks are describing systems running inside daily operations, where the person only steps in once the work is mostly done.

body.head: Where it already breaks
body.text: Shinhan Bank said AI-assisted hackers, suspected to be based overseas, got into a loan broker login page this week and leaked loan amounts, income, names and phone numbers for about 25,000 customers. An industry official said the entire financial sector carries this exposure, because the attackers used AI tools to sweep for any weak platform, so every bank's customer-facing portals are now worth testing with the same kind of tool.

body.head: Two central banks agree
body.text: Christine Lagarde told the European Parliament that global AI valuations sit in a small number of firms piling on debt, with AI-related borrowing already around a quarter of credit growth to firms as they put roughly 10% of total investment into AI this year. Days later, Australia's central bank echoed the point in its own Financial Stability Review, warning about chipmakers financing the neocloud firms that buy their chips in a cycle it called more opaque and circular, and about AI trading agents that could all move the same way at once.

body.head: The thread connecting them
body.text: So pull these four stories together: AI agents are now trusted with real operational authority inside banks, the money financing AI itself is concentrated and increasingly circular, and the tools making banks faster are making attackers faster too. None of that argues against deploying agents. It argues for building the audit trail, the security budget and the kill switch at the same speed as the rollout.

body.head: One question for Monday
body.text: Watch whether South Korea's financial watchdog finds Shinhan's gap was a one-off or something other loan broker portals share. And ask the question Lagarde and the RBA are both circling this week: when a quarter of credit growth to firms is tied to the same AI trade, what happens to the banks lending into it once sentiment turns.
